Two open-access books I've written for graduate-level quantitative methods courses.

## Quantitative Foundations in Educational Research

A self-contained introduction to applied statistics for educational and social-science research: descriptive statistics, probability, sampling, inference, regression, and ANOVA. Originally written to support a master's-level methods course.

*Migration in progress — the book is being ported from its original R Bookdown source into a native Quarto book. In the meantime it remains available at the [previous site](https://zewang.netlify.app/books/quant-foundations/_book/).*

## Structural Equation Modeling Using R and Mplus

A practical introduction to structural equation modeling with worked examples in both R (`lavaan`) and Mplus. Covers measurement models, path analysis, latent variable models, model fit, and multi-group / multilevel extensions.

*Migration in progress — the book is being ported from its original R Bookdown source into a native Quarto book. In the meantime it remains available at the [previous site](https://zewang.netlify.app/books/sem/_book/).*
